_readme: Copy this file to answers.json and fill it in. answers.json is git-ignored: it is the only place the codes exist in the clear outside Firestore.
One entry per gate. 'threshold' is the word on the landing page. Every other key is a room id from ROOM_ORDER in functions/src/config/game.ts, plus 'verdict' for the accusation.

answer: the code, as you would type it, or a list of accepted ways of writing it. Each is normalised (uppercase, spaces and punctuation stripped, times kept as HH:MM) and stored only as a SHA-256 hash.
hints: exactly three, cheapest first. They cost 5, 10 and 20 minutes. The threshold has none.
evidence: the cards a solved room gives up. Each id is written to the player's file on success. 'reveal' is the text that replaces the redaction bar.

verdict.answer: the id of one suspect in scripts/content/rooms.ts. verdict.rebuttals: for each of the others, why it was not them. verdict.evidence: the closing account, whose id is VERDICT_DOSSIER.account and whose title is that suspect's name.
Then run: npm run seed:emulator   or   npm run answers:seal and commit answers.sealed.json, so the deploy can open it.

hints: Second hint. Most of the working.

evidence.title: Time of death
evidence.body: What the detective now knows, in one line.

evidence.title: Cause of death
evidence.body: What the detective now knows, in one line.

rebuttals.another-suspect-id: Why it was not them. Shown only to a detective who names them.

evidence.title: The suspect's name, exactly as it is on the wall
evidence.body: What happened. A blank line starts a new paragraph.
